subject: Everfield: brief sync or hold demo until planning committee?
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Liam Carter <liam.carter@everfield.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-01T09:18:00-08:00
Subject: Everfield demo — proposed slot next Thursday

Hi Liam,

Thanks again for the time last week — helped me understand the query volume and the latency targets you mentioned. We had penciled in a 60-minute walkthrough + Q&A for next Thursday (Dec 9) at 10am PT. I wanted to confirm whether that still works for your team.

If Dec 9 is tight, happy to offer a 20–30 minute technical briefing this week (overview + architecture Q&A) to keep momentum while you finalize budget windows.

Attached is the deck I planned to use and the RFP you shared — thought it might be helpful to review beforehand.

Next steps: confirm full demo on Dec 9 or tell me which of these you'd prefer: (A) short sync this week, (B) move full demo to post-planning committee (Dec 15+), or (C) put demo on hold and I’ll follow up after your FY reset.

Cheers,
Ben
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood-demo-deck.pdf (pdf)]

From: Liam Carter <liam.carter@everfield.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@everfield.com>, Elise Morgan <elise.morgan@everfield.com>
Date: 2026-12-01T11:02:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Everfield demo — proposed slot next Thursday

Hey Ben — appreciate the flexibility. Quick update from our side: the executive team is on a regional roadshow the week of Dec 6–10 (CFO and Head of Product are both in-market meetings) so we’ll have a compressed calendar. On top of that, the planning committee reconvenes on Dec 14 to lock FY allocations — procurement has been asked to pause vendor demos that require capex approval until after that meeting.

That said, I don’t want to lose momentum. Option (A) — a 20–30 minute technical briefing this week — would be ideal to keep stakeholders abreast. Could you do Wed Dec 2 at 9:30am PT?

Also looped in Elise from procurement — she’ll be the point person for any procurement docs/approval timelines.

Thanks,
Liam
Senior Manager, Platform Engineering
Everfield Health
[Quoted: Attachment: Everfield_RFP.pdf]

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Liam Carter <liam.carter@everfield.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-01T12:07:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Everfield demo — proposed slot next Thursday

Liam — thanks for the heads up and for looping Elise. Wed Dec 2 at 9:30am PT works for a 25-minute briefing. I’ll keep it focused:
- 10-min quick product/architecture overview tailored to your latency/cost questions
- 10-min Q&A for engineering + procurement (KV caching, dedicated capacity, private deployment options)
- 5-min next steps & mutual action plan (timeline to full demo post-Dec 14)

For procurement, Monica will join the briefing to walk through pricing models and draft SOW cadence. Laura will cover observability and rollout controls.

If procurement would like a redline-ready SOW before the planning committee, we can prepare a draft to share by Dec 10 — can Elise confirm the preferred contract timeline?

Meeting invite sent — see calendar.

Best,
Ben
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood-demo-deck.pdf (pdf)]

On Wed, Dec 1, 2026 at 11:02 AM Liam Carter <liam.carter@everfield.com> wrote:
> Hey Ben — appreciate the flexibility...

From: Elise Morgan <elise.morgan@everfield.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Liam Carter <liam.carter@everfield.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-02T08:44:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Everfield demo — proposed slot next Thursday

Hi all — thanks for the quick turnaround. We’ll join the 9:30am PT slot. A couple procurement notes to set expectations:
- Planning committee will finalize allocations on Dec 14; anything requiring FY capex approval will be reviewed after that date.
- If you can provide a draft SOW and a high-level runbook (data controls, retention, KMS options) by Dec 10, procurement can flag any major non-starters prior to the committee.
- We may need a short commercial term (credit/extended trial) to keep the project active through the freeze in case approvals slip — that’s something to discuss after the briefing.

Elise
Senior Procurement Specialist
Everfield Health
[Attachment: none]

On Tue, Dec 1, 2026 at 12:07 PM Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com> wrote:
> Liam — thanks for the heads up and for looping Elise...

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Elise Morgan <elise.morgan@everfield.com>, Liam Carter <liam.carter@everfield.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-05T16:02:00-08:00
Subject: Follow-up & conditional plan for post-committee full demo

Elise / Liam / team — thanks again for joining the briefing on Dec 2 (great questions). Per your ask, Monica and I have put together: (1) a draft SOW (for review), (2) a two-week extended pilot credit proposal to keep the POC active if approvals slip, and (3) a concise runbook on data controls and KMS options. Links attached below.

Proposed conditional plan:
- If planning committee approves capex on Dec 14: schedule full 60-min demo + exec Q&A for week of Dec 15–19.
- If committee asks for additional info / defers: we’ll hold the full demo and apply the 2-week pilot credit to keep your sandbox active; we’ll reconvene Jan 4 for a refreshed walkthrough.

Monica — can you confirm the SOW version we sent (v1.2) is redline-ready? Stephanie — ok to approve the 2-week credit on Ben’s recommendation for this deal?

Thanks team — I’ll circle back after Dec 14 with confirmed dates or to trigger the credit.

Regards,
Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
[Attachments: EVR_SOW_v1.2.docx (docx), redwood-runbook-kms.pdf (pdf)]
